Callers: only triggarr/startup.py:160 (validate_connections at startup) calls it directly. Subclasses RadarrClient, SonarrClient and LidarrClient inherit it unchanged. Every enabled *arr instance runs this path once per startup, and in routes.py wherever a client is rebuilt after a settings save.

No tests assert on either log string (grep for 'Unexpected HTTP error' and 'Unexpected API response format' finds only base.py), so the suite will not catch this regression in either direction. test_clients.py:1075-1103 (403 and 502) exercise the HTTP branch but check only the boolean result.

Convention conflict: the same file still sanitizes in _request_with_retry (base.py:71-75: 'HTTP {status}' or the exception type name). The scheduler and engine use _sanitize_exc with explicit CR-01 comments explaining why raw httpx and pydantic text is not logged. This diff makes validate_connection the one outlier.

Redaction backstop: the loguru sinks (triggarr/logging.py) redact exact secret strings only (the *arr api_keys plus auth password_hash, api_key and session_secret). The X-Api-Key header never appears in str(HTTPStatusError), so the API key itself does not leak. The uncovered cases are URL userinfo credentials, internal hostnames, and upstream response fragments in ValidationError input_value.
No schema, migration or persisted-state impact. Performance impact is negligible: one extra str() on an error path that runs once per instance at startup.

Verdict: this is not functionally breaking, but it reverses a deliberate logging-sanitization control. I recommend reverting to the status-code and error-count messages, or using _sanitize_exc. If more diagnostic detail was the goal, log `exc.request.url.path` (no host or userinfo) and `exc.response.status_code`.

findings.fix_hint: If richer diagnostics are wanted, extract only the specific safe fields (status code, reason phrase) rather than the raw exception object, matching the pattern already used two methods above in `_request_with_retry` (lines 66-77 of this file), which deliberately logs `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` instead of the exception itself.
findings.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'Never log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII, auth headers).' The diff replaces `status=exc.response.status_code` with `exc=exc`, so `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` (method/URL/status line) is now logged wholesale instead of a single safe field. I verified the API key here is sent via the `X-Api-Key` header (not the URL) and that `httpx.HTTPStatusError.__str__` only renders the status line and URL, not headers — so no secret is directly embedded in this particular exception's message today. I could not fully rule out that a future/alternate request path (different query params, redirects, proxies) could place something sensitive in the URL that would now get logged where it previously wouldn't.
findings.title: Full exception object interpolated into log line replaces status-code-only extraction
findings.why_it_matters: The project ships a custom redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py) explicitly built to catch 'API keys that appear in httpx exception messages or stack traces,' which is direct evidence the team has previously worried about exactly this failure mode. This diff reintroduces broader exception serialization in one call site while the sibling call site in the same class intentionally avoids it, so the two most similar code paths in the file now disagree on how much exception detail is safe to log.

findings.fix_hint: Prefer `exc.error_count()` plus field names (`[e['loc'] for e in exc.errors()]`) over the raw ValidationError string, which embeds the actual input values that failed validation.
findings.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'Never log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII, auth headers).' The diff replaces `count=exc.error_count()` with `exc=exc`. Pydantic v2's `ValidationError.__str__` includes `input_value=...` for each error, which for a missing/invalid field reproduces the raw dict that failed validation — here the full `/system/status` JSON response body. Today that model (`SystemStatus`) only declares a `version` field and the response is Radarr/Sonarr's status payload (version, OS flags, branch, etc.), which I did not find to contain tokens/PII — but I could not exhaustively confirm no sensitive field is ever present in that payload across all supported *arr apps/versions, and this path will log the full raw dict for any future caller that validates a richer model.
findings.title: Full pydantic ValidationError (including raw input payload) now logged instead of error count
findings.why_it_matters: This is mitigated in practice by the redacting sink in triggarr/logging.py, which replaces any literal secret value (collected via `collect_secrets()`) in the fully-formatted log line before it reaches stderr or the web log buffer — so currently-configured API keys/passwords would still be caught even if they ended up here. The residual risk is scoped to any sensitive value that isn't in that known-secrets list (e.g. a field in a future response model, or a value not round-tripped through SecretStr), which would log the literal value with no backstop.
